items.q: Why isn't a quiet rest on the sofa a substitute for sleep?
items.a: N1 / N2 / N3 / REM chemistry **cannot be faked awake**. A "perfect" night is **~4–5 cycles of ~90 min** (first cycle often **105–110 min**), totaling **7.5–8 hours**.

items.q: What happens if you go to bed later than usual?
items.a: You **miss** the first-cycle window — it is **clock-tied, not delayable**. Early slow-wave sleep is the **GH bolus**, protein synthesis, adenosine→ATP rebuild (~**20 min**), and the **bilge-pump** wash of misfolded proteins.

items.q: What writes last night's learning to long-term storage?
items.a: **Sleep spindles** (N2, 10–15 Hz) write hippocampal "RAM" to cortical "disk." If you learned something new and spindles **do not rise**, sleep will not incorporate it. Late-night **REM** sews schema — Poe's account of insight.

items.q: Why does anxious pre-sleep make nightmares worse?
items.a: **Locus coeruleus** (norepinephrine) is **fully silent only in REM**, which divorces emotion from the N2 memory. If LC stays on (anxiety, PTSD), REM **re-sews** heart-rate/sweat into the story. Enter sleep **calm**; skip novelty, games, and **alcohol** (REM + spindle suppressant).
